taskPacket.objective: The stale-group signal guard already present in this tree (sealed from the previous run's worker, whose sandbox could not run process-signalling tests) is reviewed against its decisions, corrected where needed, and lands with the controller running the termination tests outside any sandbox.
instructions: The change this packet describes is ALREADY in the tree: the previous run's worker implemented it (src/engine/process-identity.mjs, the edits in src/engine/process.mjs, run-command.mjs, verify.mjs, cancel.mjs, recover.mjs, src/run/lock.mjs, and the new tests in test/run/process.test.mjs and test/run/lock.test.mjs), the controller sealed it as commit 4c7f237, and the orchestrator ran the node's verification command outside the sandbox: it passes in 51 seconds. That worker never reported done because inside the dsh sandbox the termination tests hang: the sandbox does not let the worker signal other processes or read `ps`, so a test waiting for a child to die waits forever. Do not repeat that. You may run `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc` and `node --test test/repo/source-shape.test.mjs` yourself; do NOT run test/run/, test/engine/seal-before-kill.test.mjs, test/engine/unfreezable.test.mjs or test/engine/supervise.test.mjs -- the controller runs them as this node's verification after you report, outside the sandbox.

Review the change with `git diff fcad2d4 -- src test` against these decisions and fix anything that violates them: (1) `invocationOwned(invocation, {child})` in src/engine/process-identity.mjs returns true only when `process.kill(pid, 0)` succeeds (EPERM is not ours) and either a live child handle (`exitCode === null && signalCode === null`) or a recorded processStartToken that still equals `processStartToken(pid)` proves identity; a null token with no handle is false. (2) `signalInvocation` never throws: ESRCH and EPERM both mean 'not ours or gone', it returns whether a signal was delivered, and terminateProcess/terminateInvocation stop escalating when nothing was delivered. (3) terminateProcess passes the job's live child handle; terminateInvocation, cancel and recovery rely on the token; an unverifiable-but-alive invocation is recorded once as an `invocation_identity_unverifiable` event line, never a new state or error code. (4) src/engine/run-command.mjs records `processStartToken(pid)` for verification children and verify.mjs carries it through. (5) darwin `processStartToken` retries once after 20 ms when `ps -o lstart=` is empty for a live pid. (6) Every module keeps its header comment; process.mjs stays under 800 lines (it is 774); no duplicated helper body; tsc clean with noUnusedLocals.

Read the new tests in test/run/process.test.mjs and test/run/lock.test.mjs and confirm they cover: invocationOwned true for a fresh detached child and false after it exits; a fabricated token on a live pid (process.pid) makes it false; terminateInvocation on process.pid with a fabricated token neither signals nor throws; an injected kill throwing EPERM does not propagate; processStartToken(process.pid) is a non-empty string on darwin and linux. Add any missing case. If you change a test, keep it free of process-signalling of the runner's own group.
If the review finds nothing to fix, report done with a summary that lists what you verified and states that the controller's verification is the proof; an empty diff is a valid outcome for this node.
decisions: A process group is signalled only with proof of ownership: a live child handle or a matching start token; null token plus no handle means unverifiable, never 'alive'.
EPERM from process.kill is 'not ours', handled like ESRCH, and never propagates out of the drive loop.
Verification children record a start token like workers do; darwin's ps-based token retries once across the spawn race.
The regression tests use the test runner's own pid with a fabricated token: a wrong implementation kills the suite, a right one does nothing.
The worker does not run process-signalling tests inside the dsh sandbox; the controller's verification is the proof.
nonGoals: Do not run test/run/, seal-before-kill, unfreezable or supervise tests yourself: they hang in the sandbox and the previous worker stalled twice doing exactly that.
Do not change stall or wall-clock timeout semantics, the seal, or the supervisor's relaunch rules.
Do not add a new node state or error code; one event string is enough.
Never run npm install in the worktree; never run the whole suite yourself.

taskPacket.objective: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/feliperun/faberun/main/install.sh | sh` installs faberun on a fresh machine into the same home layout the self-updater uses, checks the requirements first, and hands off to `faberun setup`.
instructions: Read the 'Install layout' and 'Distribution' decisions in docs/campaigns/become-faberun/spec/SPEC.md, src/host/home.mjs (the layout the script must match exactly: versions/<v>, current, and the bin symlink), src/cli/update.mjs (how the updater verifies a version) and the line grammar in DESIGN.md.

Write install.sh at the repository root: `#!/bin/sh`, `set -eu`, POSIX only (no arrays, no `[[`, no `local` assumptions beyond what dash and bash share), idempotent. Environment: FABERUN_HOME (default `$HOME/.faberun`), FABERUN_BIN_DIR (default `$HOME/.local/bin`), FABERUN_VERSION (a tag such as `v0.4.0`, `0.4.0`, or `main`), FABERUN_INSTALL_SOURCE (a path to a `.tar.gz` or to a directory to copy from, for offline installs and tests), FABERUN_NO_SETUP (skip the final setup). Steps: (1) requirements -- `node` on PATH with major version 22 or newer (`node -p 'process.versions.node'`), `tar`, and `curl` only when downloading; each failure prints `[fail] <name> · <what is missing and how to get it>` and exits 1, each success `[ok] <name> · <detail>`; (2) resolve the version: FABERUN_VERSION when set; otherwise the `tag_name` of `https://api.github.com/repos/feliperun/faberun/releases/latest` parsed with sed (no jq); when the API answers 404 or no tag parses, fall back to `main` and say so with `[warn] release · no release yet · installing main`; (3) fetch: a tag downloads `https://github.com/feliperun/faberun/archive/refs/tags/<tag>.tar.gz`, `main` downloads `.../archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz`, FABERUN_INSTALL_SOURCE uses the local tarball or directory instead; extract with `tar -xzf <file> --strip-components=1 -C <home>/versions/<version>.partial` (GitHub tarballs have one top-level directory), then rename the partial directory to `<home>/versions/<version>` (remove an existing same-version directory first so a re-run refreshes it); (4) `chmod +x <dir>/bin/faberun.mjs`, repoint `<home>/current` (symlink, replaced atomically through a temporary name and `mv -f`), and link `<bin dir>/faberun` to `<home>/current/bin/faberun.mjs`; (5) verify with `<bin dir>/faberun --version` and print `[ok] installed · faberun <printed version> · <bin dir>/faberun`; (6) when `<bin dir>` is not in PATH print `[warn] path · add <bin dir> to PATH` with the shell line to add; (7) unless FABERUN_NO_SETUP is set, when stdin and stdout are terminals, exec `<bin dir>/faberun setup`; otherwise print `next · faberun setup`. Use only `printf`, never `echo -e`; quote every path.

Write test/host/install-sh.test.mjs: build a tarball from the current tree with `tar -czf` containing a single top-level directory `faberun-test/` holding bin/, src/, skills/, integrations/ and package.json (spawnSync tar with `-s` or `--transform` is not portable, so create a temp staging directory named faberun-test, copy those paths into it with cpSync, and tar the staging parent); run `sh install.sh` with FABERUN_INSTALL_SOURCE pointing at the tarball, FABERUN_HOME and FABERUN_BIN_DIR in temp directories, FABERUN_VERSION set to the package.json version, FABERUN_NO_SETUP=1, and PATH inherited; assert `versions/<version>/bin/faberun.mjs` exists, `current` is a symlink to that directory, `<bin>/faberun` is a symlink to `current/bin/faberun.mjs`, `<bin>/faberun --version` prints `faberun <version>`, and stdout has `[ok] installed`; run it again and assert the same state (idempotent); run with FABERUN_INSTALL_SOURCE pointing at the staging directory instead of the tarball; run with a PATH that lacks node (withEmptyPath from test/helpers.mjs, keeping /bin and /usr/bin for sh and tar) and assert exit 1 with `[fail] node`. No test reaches the network.

This is the third run of this packet. Run one produced a working script whose candidate verification was killed by an unrelated engine race (fixed by the node this one depends on). Run two was rejected by the judge on one major finding, which you must not repeat: install.sh repointed `current` with `ln -s "versions/$version" "$home/current.tmp" && mv -f "$home/current.tmp" "$home/current"`. `mv` stats its destination and follows the symlink, so when `current` already points at an existing version directory the temporary link is moved INTO that directory as `current/current.tmp` and `current` keeps pointing at the old version -- every upgrade on an existing install is a no-op. Repoint with `ln -sfn "versions/$version" "$home/current"` (the -n/-h flag stops ln from following an existing link; both BSD and GNU ln accept -sfn), and give the same treatment to the `$bin_dir/faberun` link. The test suite must cover the upgrade: install version A, then run the script again with FABERUN_VERSION set to a version B built from a second staging directory whose package.json says B, and assert `current` now resolves to versions/B and `<bin>/faberun --version` prints B.
Run the verification commands yourself in the foreground with explicit timeouts and fix what they report before reporting done. Do not run the whole suite; the controller does.
decisions: POSIX sh, set -eu, idempotent, no jq; GitHub archive tarballs by tag, main as the pre-release fallback.
The layout is the one src/host/home.mjs defines; the updater and the installer must agree.
Verification is the installed binary printing its own version before the script reports success.
The script hands off to faberun setup on an interactive terminal unless FABERUN_NO_SETUP is set.
nonGoals: No checksum or signature verification in this version (recorded as a follow-up).
Never run npm install in the worktree; never run the whole suite yourself.
